newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firmer as IPE gains, but buying slack.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firmer as IPE gains, but buying slack.

text.p: NWE gas oil was firmer on Thursday as futures made $2.00 gains, but barge premiums eased amid scant buying interest.
Benchmark IPE gas oil futures were trading $2.25 a tonne higher at $178.50 at 1129 GMT.
On the Rotterdam barge market, offers dipped to $2.00/$2.25 a tonne over June IPE, with bids at +$1.25. Buyers held out for June IPE +$1.00 for early June with offers at +$1.50-$1.75.
Buying in the German heating oil market was poor. "Germany is a pure disaster because of lack of demand.. I think premiums will come down further in the coming days," said one dealer.
Diesel barges were fairly steady at June IPE +$9.00/$10.00 a tonne fob ARA.
On the cargo market, a small DIN cargo was traded firmer on Wednesday at June IPE +5.75 cif Bremen for end-May delivery.
But traders said they expected next deals to be softer.
"(The buyer) had a short to cover and had to pay up for a cargo before the end of May," a trader said.
June 1-10 DIN cargoes were pegged at June IPE +$3.00-$5.00 cif Hamburg.
